title: Navy, Shield AI pour big bucks into X-BAT drone development
key_facts: Shield AI and the US Navy are putting another $300 million into the X-BAT vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) drone, the firm announced on 8 Oct 2026.
The Navy approved a $150 million modification to an existing Other Transaction agreement; Shield AI is matching it with $150 million of its own capital.
Together with $100 million announced earlier, the combined investment is $400 million.
X-BAT is slated for flight testing later this year; Shield AI says it has completed engine light-off and thrust-vectoring nozzle integration.
Shield AI markets it as the 'world's first AI-piloted VTOL fighter jet', 26 feet long with a range of more than 2,000 nautical miles, per the company.
The Navy wants a drone that can launch from ships without large flight decks for long-range strikes.
Production is planned in the Seattle area, with testing in Newton, Kansas.
quote_evidence: Altogether, Shield AI and the US Navy are investing a combined $400 million in the X-BAT drone, which is slated for flight testing later this year.

The Navy has signed off on a $150 million modification to an existing Other Transaction agreement for the X-BAT program under the Pentagon’s Defense Exportability Features program, and Shield AI has agreed to match that funding with $150 million of its own capital, according to the firm.

The effort comes as the Navy has sought an unmanned aerial system (UAS) capable of launching from ships without large flight decks — like Arleigh Burke-class destroyers — to conduct long-range strikes.
why_it_matters_hint: Shows the Navy paying for an AI-flown combat drone that could operate from smaller ships.
notes: Funding terms and aircraft specifications are Shield AI's, per the firm.
